issues.title: Wayfinder map: Remove the local-repo backing from CVM courses
issues.body:
## Destination

Remove CVM's local-git-repo backing of courses **entirely**. No `CourseRepo`, no on-disk section/lesson folders, no ghost/real distinction, no materialization cascade, no git plumbing. Every **Section / Lesson / Video** becomes a plain DB row; a video's local files live in **one directory keyed by `lineageId`** (the Standalone-Video model, unified across all videos). **Publish** derives structure from the DB and emits **only `.mp4` + `course.json`** to Dropbox.

**Reached when:** every decision needed to write an implementation spec is locked — the schema/data-model changes, publish output, per-video file-storage model, `todo`/changelog treatment, the one-time migration, the #1190 sequencing, the agent VFS model (resolved: agent deleted), the `git-push` dependency, and the `course.json` path shape (resolved: `path` retired in favour of `title`) — **all settled below; no tickets remain open.** What's left is spec-writing + execution, which is out of scope for this map.

## Notes

- **Target repo:** `~/repos/matt/course-video-manager` (CVM). Code refs are `origin/main`.
- **Skills:** consult `/grilling` + `/domain-modeling` on every ticket; ground any new terms in CVM `CONTEXT.md`.
- **This effort supersedes the tail of the title-driven-paths work** (map #1181 / PR #1190): it keeps slices 1–3 but makes the `git mv` slices (4 & 6) dead. Coordinate before that PR's owner finishes them.
- **Ground truth already established by investigation (do not re-derive):**
  - The on-disk backing is concentrated in ~10 core service files that mostly *delete* (`course-repo-write-service.ts` = all git shell-outs, `course-repo-parser.ts`, `course-repo-sync-validation.ts`, `course-write-materialize-ops.ts`, `git-status-service.server.ts`), plus ~20 UI files and ~30 test files. Est. ~50–55 non-test source files touch ghost/real.
  - `courses.filePath` (DB `repo_path`, nullable) = the repo pointer; `lessons.fsStatus` (ghost/real) + biconditional CHECK with `authoringStatus`; section real-ness is **derived** (`sectionHasRealLessons`), never stored.
  - `videos` has both a per-version `id` and a stable `lineageId` (`NOT NULL`, `$defaultFn(randomUUID)`); `copyVersionStructure` clones videos with a **new `id`, same `lineageId`**; `course.json` already keys videos by `lineageId`.
  - Standalone videos already use a per-video dir `standalone-video-files/{id}` (gitignored, never published); both standalone + lesson videos already share the `files[]` read contract in `video-posting-context.server.ts`.
  - `course.json` (`buildCourseJson`) is written to the Dropbox course dir on **every** publish; already carries per-video `body` + SEO `description` + `hash` + `chapters`; **no transcript field**. AI Hero does **not** yet read it.
  - The in-app changelog is computed live from DB versions; the Dropbox `changelog.md` is a redundant dump.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->

- [Remove the local-repo backing entirely — no feature flag](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1198) — **remove wholesale**, no flag/mode (a flag freezes the exact complexity being removed); safety net is git history + the migration; no new repo-backed courses; reintroduce per-video dirs later if code exercises ever return.
- [Publish output: .mp4 + course.json only](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1199) — Publish emits **only `.mp4` + `course.json`** to Dropbox; drop `.transcript.md`/`.body.md`/`.meta.json`/`TODO.md`/`changelog.md`; **transcript stays out** (CMS pipeline owns it); publish derives structure from the DB, not the repo.
- [Keep todo/done as a free per-lesson flag](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1200) — `todo`/`done` becomes a plain nullable column **decoupled from filesystem** (drop the biconditional CHECK); keep the in-app changelog (computed from DB); only loss is the unread `TODO.md`.
- [Unify per-video local files, keyed by lineageId](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1201) — one **`video-files/{lineageId}`** store for **all** videos → versioning copies **zero files**; collapses the lesson-vs-standalone branch; drop `videos.filePath`; rename `standalone-video-files` → `video-files`.
- [Migration: DB-only + rename standalone dirs](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1202) — drop `repo_path`/`fs_status`/biconditional/`videos.filePath`, move uniqueness to `order`; rename `{id}`→`{lineageId}` dirs; former ghosts default `todo`; **on-disk repos left untouched**, stale Dropbox cleaned by next publish's sweep.
- [Sequencing with #1190 title-driven paths](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1203) — land #1190 **slices 1–3**, **cancel slices 4 & 6** (dead git-mv/folder-normalization), fold slice 5 into this migration; repo-removal rides on top. ACTION: notify #1190's owner.
- [Confirm no live dependency on git-push to a student repo](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1205) — **no live dependency; nothing replaces it.** The Push button (`git-push` route + `GitPushMenuItem` + `gitStatus` loader) is vestigial → just delete it; old on-disk repos stay inert (per #1202) and get hand-edited in the rare case.
- [Agent VFS model without ghost/real or materialize](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1204) — **delete the agent entirely** (CVM CLI covers the editing surface), so there's no post-removal VFS contract to spec. Self-contained, orthogonal to repo-backing: drops the agent route + `features/course-agent/**` + `services/vfs/**` + `?agentPanel` mount + prototype route + course-agent decision-map docs; touches no shared service/field/migration. CLI-parity gaps (section/chapter/clip-text writes, lesson/video soft-delete) are consciously accepted losses, not follow-ups. Deletion folds into the repo-backing implementation spec.
- [`course.json` path shape now that it's CMS-facing](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1206) — **retire `path`; identify every node by `title`.** `path` was a folder name that baked ordering (`NN`/`NN.MM`) into an identifier; ordering already lives in `order`. Drop `path` from the emitted `course.json`; identity = `title` + stable `id` (`lineageId`); videos located by `hash`. Schema: rename `sections.path`→`title` (backfill raw slug, flag for manual retitle), rename `videos.path`→`title` (holds `explainer`/`problem`/`solution`), drop `lessons.path` (clean `title` already exists). Uniqueness moves off `path` (per #1202).

## Not yet specified

- **Standalone ↔ lesson relationship & the `move-to-course` flow.** With dirs keyed by `lineageId`, moving a standalone video onto a lesson is just setting `lessonId` (no file move), and `_app.videos.$videoId.move-to-course.tsx` largely dissolves. Whether the standalone/lesson UI distinction changes at all wants a pass — now a pure CLI/UI concern (the agent is gone, per #1204).
- **Publish-time validation/lint that assumed disk structure** (`DoesNotExistOnDbError`, sync-validation) — what, if anything, replaces it once structure comes from the DB.

## Out of scope

- **Writing the implementation spec + making the code changes.** This map ends at locked decisions; execution is a separate effort.
- **Footage path** (`videos.originalFootagePath`) and exported-`.mp4` hashing/handling — unaffected by repo removal. (Note: `videos.path` was *mistakenly* listed here as a footage path — it's actually the video's title; brought into scope and resolved by #1206.)
- **The AI Hero-side `course.json` reader** — different repo (`~/repos/ai/course-builder`), future work.

issues.title: Wayfinder map: TikTok creator — short-form videos, portrait player, subtitled render, TikTok + Shorts posting
issues.body:
## Destination

A **decision-complete spec** for a "TikTok creator" inside CVM — enough locked decisions that an implementation agent could build it without further design. In scope to decide:

- **Short-form videos as normal Videos** — same `videos` table, marked by an **explicit attribute** (not a new entity; seeded from the existing portrait/`profile` signal, but intent-driven and overridable). Low-friction, standalone, **no Pitch relationship**.
- A **portrait "creator" view / player** — the "new style of video player" (9/16), styled differently from the landscape lesson modal.
- A **subtitled-vertical render pipeline** — "turn it into a real thing" = produce a finished, captioned, vertical `.mp4`, reusing the Remotion + OBS→subtitle prior art in `~/repos/ts/total-typescript-monorepo`.
- **Posting to TikTok + YouTube Shorts** — TikTok is the genuinely-new integration (YouTube upload already exists as landscape posting).

**Reached when:** every decision an implementation spec needs is locked — the attribute shape, the creator/player UI, the low-friction creation flow, the render/caption pipeline, and the TikTok + Shorts posting lifecycle — with the third-party API facts researched. **Execution (writing the spec's code) is out of scope.**

## Notes

- **Target repo:** `~/repos/matt/course-video-manager` (CVM). Prior-art repo: `~/repos/ts/total-typescript-monorepo` (deprecated; contains the OBS→subtitle CLI + a Remotion project).
- **Skills:** consult `/grilling` + `/domain-modeling` on every ticket; ground any new terms in CVM `CONTEXT.md`.
- **Ground truth already established (do not re-derive):**
  - **"TikTok"/"Portrait" already exists at the Clip level** via `Clip.profile` (OBS tags it at record time). `getIsClipPortrait()` = `profile === "TikTok" || "Portrait"`; the video-editor already renders those clips 9/16. Vertical-ness flows through from recording — it is not bolted on.
  - The **Video** entity (`app/db/schema.ts`) has **no** orientation/aspect field; portrait is currently derived from clips.
  - **YouTube upload already fully exists**: `youtube-upload-service.ts` (resumable), Google OAuth, `youtubeAuth` table, posting UI at `_app.videos.$videoId.post.tsx`. **No TikTok integration exists.**
  - The existing **video player** (`app/components/video-player.tsx`) is a bare landscape `<video>` modal (native controls, 1.75×, audio boost) — no portrait handling.
  - `shortsDirectoryOutputName` param in `video-processing-service.exportVideoClips()` is scaffolded but unused.
  - **Pitch** = heavyweight pre-planning packaging artifact (copy/thumbnail/effort/priority) for Standalone Videos, feeds the Deliverables Calendar. TikTok videos deliberately **bypass** this (low friction).
- **Stack:** React Router v7 (file routes), Effect services, Drizzle + Postgres. Features under `app/features/`, services under `app/services/`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->

- [Low-friction creation flow + top-level TikTok list](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1268) — creation is one **record tile** (invisible shell + existing OBS record flow, AI names/describes from transcript); the list is a dedicated **"TikToks" top-level sidebar surface** as a portrait 9:16 gallery grid (prototype Variant B). Status-badge data source deferred to #1274.

- [Portrait creator view / player](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1267) — the creator view is the **"Studio" built on the real video-editor**: keep the editor's **left (clip timeline) + center (Beats) untouched**; **replace the player-heavy right column** (`VideoPlayerPanel`) with a **video-forward, height-driven 9/16 preview** and a **header bar above it** (chosen "Variant A") holding a primary **Post** button + an **"Actions ▾"** dropdown **copied from `actions-dropdown.tsx`** (curated to Render vertical / Post TikTok / Post Shorts / Copy / Export / Rename / Reveal). **No in-app caption editing** (Remotion captions downstream). Build reuses the reducers (`use-video-editor.ts`) + pure selectors + `PreloadableClip` (lift `PreloadableClipManager` to prop-driven). Prototype: branch `worktree-tiktok-portrait-player-1267`, commit `86e7e1d4`.

- [Short-form attribute: how a Video is marked as a TikTok/short](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1266) — `format: standard | short` enum on `videos` (`NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard'`, matching `pauseType`/`beats.kind` house-style). Names **form-factor, not destination** (destinations are many → posting model #1274). **Human-set intent**: no seed from `Clip.profile`, no backfill (existing rows default to `standard`). A `short` is always a **Standalone Video** (`lessonId = NULL`). Must be **filterable + per-row badged** in the standalone list; exact layout (filter vs tabs vs separate list) deferred to a **prototype under #1268**.

- [Research: TikTok upload API](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1269) — it's the **Content Posting API** (Login Kit OAuth; GA 2026), with **Direct Post** (`video.publish`) vs **Upload-to-Inbox/Draft** (`video.upload`). ⚠️ **Dominant constraint: unaudited apps are locked to `SELF_ONLY` visibility (~5 users/24h) — you cannot post publicly until you pass TikTok's audit, which requires building their mandated posting-UX/Content-Sharing-Guidelines.** Upload = chunked `FILE_UPLOAD` (5–64MB chunks, ≤128MB, or `PULL_FROM_URL` needing DNS domain verification). Flow: `creator_info/query` → `init` → upload → `status/fetch`. Video: MP4/MOV, ≤4GB/≤10min, caption ≤2200 runes; `privacy_level` must match live `creator_info`. Findings: `docs/research/tiktok-upload-api.md` (branch `worktree-agent-a57ce875e7a76d1ab`).
- [Research: monorepo / Remotion audit](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1272) — the Remotion project (`apps/remotion-subtitle-renderer`) is **already fully decoupled** (zero `@total-typescript/*` imports); it renders a **transparent 1080×1920 subtitle+CTA overlay** (not the final video), which the `tt` CLI then ffmpeg-overlays onto the clip. Subtitles come from **OpenAI Whisper** (`whisper-1`, word timings); captions are styled in React/Tailwind. **CVM already shells out to `tt` via `app/services/tt-cli-service.ts` (= current option c).** Recommendation: **port/inline `MyComp` into CVM** and drive `@remotion/renderer` programmatically (~2–4 days) to shed the deprecated monorepo; standalone-extract ≈ ½ day. ⚠️ Committed AWS keys found in that repo's `.env` — rotate. Findings: `docs/research/ttmonorepo-remotion-audit.md` (branch `worktree-agent-a9977c2958ed2a3fa`).
- [Research: multi-platform posting feasibility](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1271) — every platform has a usable upload API; the gate is the differentiator. **Cheap fan-out:** X/Twitter (v2 chunked, no review, ~$0.015/post) and Bluesky (AT Protocol, free, no review) are LOW-cost fast follows; LinkedIn is MEDIUM–HIGH (Community Management approval); **Instagram/FB Reels is HIGH** (Meta App Review + business verification) — defer, poor reward at low following. Recommended order: X → Bluesky → LinkedIn → Threads → defer Meta → skip Pinterest. Findings: `docs/research/multi-platform-posting-feasibility.md` (branch `worktree-agent-a4f714c62b7813545`). *(Building these stays out of scope.)*
- [Research: YouTube Shorts posting](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1270) — **no API flag exists**; YouTube *infers* a Short from the file (vertical/square, ≤3 min as of Dec 2025); `#Shorts` is advisory only. CVM's existing uploader (`youtube-upload-service.ts`, generic resumable `videos.insert`, `youtube.upload` scope) is already Short-capable with **no landscape assumptions**. Real gap is **upstream**: CVM has no vertical asset to feed it, and `upload.ts` mandates a thumbnail (`setYouTubeThumbnail`) that must be *skipped* for Shorts. Findings: `docs/research/youtube-shorts-posting.md` (branch `worktree-agent-ac67d04d58fc97003`).

- [Render/caption pipeline: how CVM produces the subtitled vertical .mp4](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1273) — **Extract Remotion `MyComp` to its own clean repo + local shell-out; CVM owns the glue.** Keep the exact Remotion caption look (non-negotiable; ffmpeg-burn rejected). Shed the deprecated monorepo (its deps are stale, the renderer isn't). CVM already owns Whisper transcription + ffmpeg natively — shell out **only** the irreducible Remotion overlay render; add the ffmpeg composite locally. Render contract = **explicit props per-invocation** (not the `meta.json`-in-source-tree handshake). Render runs **locally** (Chromium via `@remotion/renderer`); **Lambda/AWS dropped** — CVM is a local desktop tool. ⚠️ extraction must not copy the renderer `.env`; rotate its leaked AWS keys. Full inline-into-CVM deferred as optional future.
- [Posting lifecycle: idea → recorded → rendered → posted](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1274) — **Post via Buffer, not the TikTok API.** Persist only *which platforms a Video was posted to* in a new **`videoPosts`** child table (`videoId, platform, remoteId?, remoteUrl?, postedAt`); "rendered" is derived from the filesystem (does the `.mp4` exist), "idea" untracked. **One "Post" button opens a posting modal** (author/generate title + YouTube description + short-form caption/hashtags + **AI Hero short link** via the existing `ai-hero-shortlink-service`), then fires **two parallel jobs**, each writing its own row: **YouTube Shorts** via the existing direct uploader (rich row; *skip the mandatory thumbnail*), and **Buffer** (`platform="buffer"`) = drop the `.mp4` + a sidecar `.txt` caption into a **Dropbox** folder → Zapier → Buffer fans out to TikTok/X/Bluesky. Sidesteps TikTok's unaudited-`SELF_ONLY` trap entirely. Buffer/Zapier tier + cost → research #1275. ✅ **Transport superseded by #1277:** the Dropbox→Zapier→Buffer leg is replaced — >100MB posts now go **Vercel Blob → Buffer GraphQL API `createPost(assets:[url])`** (Zapier removed, Dropbox retired). The rest of #1274 (one Post button, `videoPosts` table, parallel YouTube-Shorts + Buffer jobs) stands; the Buffer job now calls the API + polls `post.status` instead of dropping a file.
- [Research: Buffer + Zapier tiers to post TikTok](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1275) — cheapest viable chain is **Buffer Free + Zapier Free = $0/mo** (10-post refillable queue/channel, ~100 tasks/mo, 15-min poll, 2-step Dropbox→Buffer Zap); scale-up = Buffer **Essentials $5/channel/mo annual** (+ Zapier Starter ~$20/mo only if a 3-step Zap / >100 posts/mo needed). Buffer Free **does** post TikTok **video** (≤1080×1920, 3s–10min, ≤1GB); auto-publish (Direct-Post) needs **original audio**. Caption via Dropbox "Include file contents" → Buffer **Text** field (partially confirmed; .mp4-attach + clean .txt-read are the joints to prototype). Findings: docs/research/buffer-zapier-tiktok-tiers.md (branch worktree-agent-a321d68fd6db8c818).
- [Task: validate Dropbox→Zapier→Buffer→TikTok chain end-to-end](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1276) — HITL run on real 1080×1920 MP4s: **Buffer Free posts TikTok** ✅ and a **Free 2-step Zap attaches a <100MB video** (File field) into Buffer's queue ✅ — but **>100MB fails via _both_ the File field _and_ the Dropbox Direct Media URL** ❌. A 75s clip was already 141MB, so real renders routinely exceed 100MB → this **partially invalidates #1274's Buffer-via-Dropbox transport**. Graduated grilling ticket #1277 to decide the >100MB transport; caption + auto-publish joints left untested → follow-up task #1278 (blocked on #1277). Tier verdict: $0/mo Buffer Free + Zapier Free holds **only for <100MB clips**.

- [Decide the >100MB TikTok posting transport](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1277) — **>100MB fix: Vercel Blob → Buffer GraphQL API; Zapier removed.** The 100MB wall was *Zapier's*, not Buffer's — Buffer's 2026 GraphQL API (`api.buffer.com`) takes video **by public URL (Buffer pulls it) → no upload-size ceiling** (~1GB TikTok cap only). Transport: render → upload to **Vercel Blob** (permanent public URL) → `createPost(assets:[url])` → poll `post(id).status` → **delete blob on `Sent`** (+24h grace; keep on `Error`). Keeps Buffer's TikTok/X/Bluesky fan-out + the audit-dodge (#1269 `SELF_ONLY` still sidestepped); **retires the Dropbox outbox** (#1276) and Zapier. Buffer fetches **at publish** (hours–days if queued) → deletion is poll-to-`Sent`, which **decouples “schedule vs now” from the transport**. Ruled out: pay-for-Buffer (wrong lever), Make.com (no middleman needed), <100MB render cap (quality/#1273 leak), direct TikTok API (#1269 audit trap). Follow-ups: verify Buffer API access on current plan (#1279); #1278 reframed to the API path.

- [Verify Buffer GraphQL API access on current plan](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1279) — **A personal API key can be minted on Buffer Free** — no Team-plan upgrade forced. The pay-for-Buffer risk from #1277 is closed. (Channel visibility + caption + publish-mode ride on the #1278 end-to-end validation, now unblocked.)

- [Task: validate caption field + auto-publish/reminder over the Buffer GraphQL API path](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1278) — **HITL run ✅ — the Vercel Blob → Buffer GraphQL → TikTok path works end-to-end.** A 141MB (>100MB) clip uploaded to Blob and was accepted by `createPost(assets:[{ video:{ url } }])`; the **caption rides as the top-level `text` field and landed verbatim** on TikTok (no sidecar `.txt`); **`schedulingType: automatic` genuinely AUTO-PUBLISHED** — the post reached `sent` on its own, *no reminder fallback* (clip had original audio); the **TikTok channel is API-visible** via `channels(input:{ organizationId })`; the blob auto-deleted on `sent`. This closes the last frontier ticket — #1277's transport + #1279's Free-tier access are now confirmed live, so the Buffer leg of #1274's posting lifecycle is fully validated. Verified API shapes: root `POST https://api.buffer.com`, `Bearer` auth, single `channelId`, post-2026-05-25 `@oneOf` `assets`, lowercase `PostStatus` (`draft|buffer|sent|error`). Harness (throwaway): branch `research/tiktok-buffer-validate-1278` (`prototypes/tiktok-buffer-validate/` + `setup-wizard.sh`).

- [OBS profile management: editor drives Landscape Recording vs TikTok profile](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/issues/1281) — **CVM actively drives the OBS profile per editor** (landscape editor → `Landscape Recording`, TikTok Studio → `TikTok`), rather than the user switching by hand. Today CVM only *reads* the profile (`GetProfileList`, `obs-connector.tsx:405`) and never sets it; the addition is `SetCurrentProfile`. OBS **blocks profile switches while any output is active** — recording, streaming, **or the virtual camera** (which runs the whole time as the live-preview source, `useConnectToOBSVirtualCamera`) — so the switch is **choreographed around the virtual cam**: `StopVirtualCam` → `SetCurrentProfile` → `StartVirtualCam` (no MediaStream re-acquire; the OBS Virtual Camera device shows a placeholder while stopped and resumes on the new profile's 9/16 canvas → Studio preview goes portrait for free). **Missing profile → error, never auto-create** (`CreateProfile` yields an empty profile with no vertical canvas). Side-effect: forcing `TikTok` makes every Studio clip portrait by construction, **dissolving the format↔clip mismatch warning** (former fog #5, now out of scope).

## Not yet specified

<!-- Empty — the way to the destination is clear. All six former fog items are dispatched: fog #3 (post-modal placement) is covered by #1267/#1274; fog #1/#2/#4/#5/#6 are ruled out of scope below. This map is decision-complete and spec-ready. -->

_(none — see Out of scope; map is spec-ready)_

## Out of scope

- **Building** Instagram / X / LinkedIn integrations — *researched* for feasibility only; no integration code this effort.
- **Writing the implementation spec's code / shipping working uploads** — this map ends at locked decisions.
- **A Pitch ↔ TikTok relationship** — ruled out; pitches are for longer-form, expensive, planned content.
- **Ideation / "set of ideas" backlog for TikToks** (former fog #1) — how a TikTok idea originates/queues; user doesn't care for this effort.
- **Caption *styling* depth** (former fog #2) — fixed vs configurable subtitle style in the render pipeline; user doesn't care for this effort. (In-app caption *editing* already ruled out in #1267.)
- **Tie to the Deliverables Calendar / changelog** (former fog #4) — whether posted TikToks surface in planning/changelog views; not needed.
- **Auto-warn on format↔clip mismatch** (former fog #5) — dissolved by #1281: the TikTok Studio forces the `TikTok` profile, so Studio clips are portrait by construction; the only mismatch left is a manual `format` override on an old landscape video, not worth a warning.
- **Persist post-page draft state (title/description/caption) to DB** (former fog #6) — currently localStorage; a general post-page improvement that also touches long-form posting → its own effort, not this spec.

issues.title: Clip Mockup Chapters for the Animatic, and delete the Mockups tab
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

An Animatic is long. A Lesson mocked at one Clip Mockup per spoken paragraph runs to sixty rows and half an hour of playback, and the Animatic page shows every one of them as a flat list in its sidebar. There is no way to see the shape of the Lesson in that list, no way to answer "which part am I watching", and no way to fold away the twenty rows of a Playthrough that are already settled so the two moments still being judged sit next to each other on screen.

A filmed Video has had the answer to this for a long time. Its timeline groups Clips under Chapters, and those Chapters collapse — individually, and all at once. The Animatic, which is the same list of moments one rung lower on the fidelity ladder, has nothing.

There is a second, smaller problem. The video editor's side panel carries a fourth tab, Mockups, which was never asked for: a second editable view of the same Clip Mockups, with inline line editing, drag-to-reorder and a delete button. It is not used, it is a second write path into a noun whose writes are otherwise a CLI, and it shares the Clip Mockup order space invisibly — a drag there can move a Clip Mockup across a boundary the author cannot see.

## Solution

Give a Video's Animatic **Clip Mockup Chapters**: named dividers that group its Clip Mockups for navigation, in the spirit of YouTube chapters. A Clip Mockup Chapter has a title and a position in the Animatic and nothing else. It is authored from the `cvm` CLI, and it shows up on the Animatic page as a divider in the sidebar, carrying its own rolled-up Clip Mockup count and run time, collapsible on its own or with every other one at a stroke. Clicking its title seeks the playhead to the first Clip Mockup under it.

Membership is implicit, exactly as a Chapter's is over Clips: a Clip Mockup belongs to the last Clip Mockup Chapter above it in the Animatic. There is no link from a Clip Mockup to a Clip Mockup Chapter to keep in step, nothing to re-parent when a row moves, and Clip Mockups above the first divider simply belong to no Chapter.

And delete the Mockups tab. After it goes, every Clip Mockup write is `cvm clip-mockup`, and the Animatic page is purely something to watch.

## User Stories

1. As Matt watching a 34-minute Animatic, I want the sidebar grouped under named Chapters, so that I can tell which part of the Lesson the playhead is in without reading sixty lines.
2. As Matt watching an Animatic, I want to collapse a Chapter I have already judged, so that the two moments I am still comparing sit next to each other on screen.
3. As Matt watching an Animatic, I want to collapse every Chapter at once, so that I can see the whole Lesson's shape as a dozen titles and decide where to look next.
4. As Matt with everything collapsed, I want one more click to expand everything again, so that getting back to the detailed view costs nothing.
5. As Matt looking at a collapsed Chapter, I want its Clip Mockup count and run time on the divider, so that "this Chapter is eleven minutes" is answerable without expanding it.
6. As Matt looking at an open Chapter, I want that same count and run time still shown, so that the number does not appear and vanish as I fold things.
7. As Matt reading a Chapter title in the sidebar, I want clicking it to seek the playhead to its first Clip Mockup, so that a collapsed Chapter is still somewhere I can jump to.
8. As Matt with a Chapter collapsed while playback runs, I want it to expand itself when the playhead enters it, so that the list never hides the row I am currently hearing.
9. As Matt watching an Animatic, I want the position badge to keep counting Clip Mockups only, so that the number I read off the screen is still the number I say out loud and the number `--at` takes.
10. As Matt watching an Animatic, I want Chapters never to appear on the canvas or add time to the playback, so that the Animatic's run time still predicts the filmed Lesson's.
11. As Matt watching an Animatic with no Chapters at all, I want the sidebar to look exactly as it does today, so that adding this feature costs nothing on a Video that does not use it.
12. As Matt watching an Animatic whose first Chapter starts at position 6, I want the first five Clip Mockups to render as plain rows above it, so that a run of unchaptered moments needs no invented heading.
13. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter add --video <id> --title "…"` to append a Chapter to the end of an Animatic, so that I can open a Chapter and then keep adding Clip Mockups into it as I author.
14. As an authoring agent, I want `--before <id>` / `--after <id>` on `add`, so that I can insert a Chapter into an Animatic I have already built.
15. As an authoring agent, I want those anchors to accept a Clip Mockup id **or** a Clip Mockup Chapter id, so that "open a Chapter right before number 14's row" is one call.
16. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter list --video <id>` as NDJSON, so that I can read back the ids I need for anchoring.
17. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter get <id…>` to be variadic, so that reading several back matches every other noun's `get`.
18. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter update <id> --title "…"`, so that I can rename a Chapter after Matt tells me the title is wrong.
19. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter move <id> --before|--after <id>`, so that I can slide a Chapter boundary when Matt says a moment belongs in the previous part.
20. As an authoring agent, I want `move` to refuse to run with no anchor, so that I cannot silently send a divider to the end of an Animatic where it means nothing.
21. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter delete <id>` to archive the Chapter and leave every Clip Mockup under it alone, so that an organisational verb can never destroy hours of frames and synthesised speech.
22. As an authoring agent deleting a Chapter, I want its Clip Mockups absorbed into the Chapter above — or left unchaptered if it was the first — so that the outcome is predictable without a rule about orphans.
23. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup list --video <id> --with-chapters` to interleave Chapter rows into the stream, so that I can see the Animatic's grouping in the same read that gives me its lines.
24. As an authoring agent reading `--with-chapters`, I want every row to carry a `type` discriminator, so that I never have to guess which kind of row I am holding.
25. As an authoring agent reading `--with-chapters`, I want every Clip Mockup row to carry an explicit `position`, so that interleaved Chapter rows cannot make me miscount the number I pass back to `--at`.
26. As an authoring agent reading `--with-chapters`, I want Chapter rows to carry `position: null`, so that it is stated rather than implied that a Chapter has no position.
27. As an authoring agent, I want bare `cvm clip-mockup list` unchanged byte for byte, so that the `jq` pipelines in the animatic skill — including the run-time sum — keep working.
28. As an authoring agent, I want `cvm clip-mockup-chapter --help` to explain the noun, the implicit membership and the shared order space, so that I can use it correctly without reading the schema.
29. As an authoring agent on the Remote Box, I want every `clip-mockup-chapter` verb to work off Matt's machine, so that I can organise an Animatic even where I cannot capture a frame or synthesise a line.
30. As an authoring agent, I want Clip Mockup Chapter writes to need no Draft Course Version, so that they behave like the Clip Mockups they group rather than like the Clips they mock.
31. As an authoring agent, I want a Chapter and a Clip Mockup to share one order key space, so that inserting a Chapter between two Clip Mockups is one write and needs no renumbering.
32. As an authoring agent, I want an unknown `--video` to be a not-found and a bad flag combination to be invalid input, so that failures carry the same exit codes as every other noun.
33. As Matt duplicating a Video, I want its Clip Mockup Chapters copied with its Clip Mockups, so that the copy's plan keeps the shape I gave the original.
34. As Matt duplicating a Video, I want the copied Chapters to sit in exactly the same places between the copied Clip Mockups, so that regenerated order keys do not pile every divider at one end.
35. As Matt committing a Course Version, I want the snapshot to carry each Video's Clip Mockup Chapters, so that an old version's Animatic still reads the way it did.
36. As Matt duplicating a whole Course, I want the same, so that all three copy paths behave alike.
37. As Matt publishing a Course, I want Clip Mockup Chapters never to reach `course.json`, so that an internal planning artifact stays internal, like a Beat and like a Clip Mockup.
38. As Matt, I want the Mockups tab gone from the video editor's side panel, so that there is one place a Clip Mockup is written and one place it is watched.
39. As Matt, I want the editor to land on the Script tab as it does today after the removal, so that deleting a tab changes nothing about how I open the editor.
40. As Matt whose browser has the Mockups tab remembered for some Video, I want it to fall back to Script silently, so that a stale saved tab is not an error.
41. As Matt, I want the "Watch the Animatic" link in the editor's header to survive the removal, so that I can still reach the player from the Video I am editing.
42. As Matt, I want the Animatic page's frames and audio to keep loading after the removal, so that deleting an unused tab cannot break the page I actually use.
43. As an agent reading the codebase later, I want a `**Clip Mockup Chapter**` entry in CONTEXT.md with its own `_Avoid_` line, so that I do not confuse it with the Chapter that groups filmed Clips.
44. As an agent reading the codebase later, I want the existing `**Chapter**` entry to warn against the confusion from its side too, so that the guard works whichever entry I land on first.
45. As an agent reading the codebase later, I want an ADR recording the divider-in-a-shared-order-space decision and the implicit-membership consequence, so that I do not redesign it as a parent id.
46. As an authoring agent reading the `animatic` skill, I want it to teach Clip Mockup Chapters as coarse navigational groupings in the spirit of YouTube chapters, so that I do not invent a taxonomy or mirror the Beats one-for-one.
47. As an authoring agent reading the `animatic` skill, I want `--with-chapters` presented as the way to read an Animatic back, so that I reason about the grouping I am writing into rather than a flat list.

## Implementation Decisions

**The noun.** A new `clip_mockup_chapter` table: id, `videoId` (cascade delete, indexed like every other Video-owned noun), `name`, `order`, `archived`, `createdAt`. It mirrors the existing `chapter` table's column shape deliberately, and has no relation to it and no foreign key into it.

**One order space, shared with Clip Mockups.** A Clip Mockup Chapter's `order` is a fractional index in the same key space as `clip_mockup.order`, exactly as a Chapter's is with a Clip's. This is the whole design. Consequences taken on purpose:

- Membership is implicit. A Clip Mockup belongs to the last Chapter above it. There is no `chapterId` on `clip_mockup`, so a reorder can never leave a stale parent behind and a Chapter can never disagree with the list.
- Positioning any of the four operations (create a Chapter, move a Chapter, create a Clip Mockup, move a Clip Mockup) must compute its key against the **merged, sorted** list of both nouns, not against one table. The existing `orderKeyBeforeItem` primitive already does exactly this for Clips and Chapters and is reused unchanged.
- Creating or moving a Clip Mockup keeps its current external behaviour — append to the end, or before a named row — but its key is now computed in the merged space, so appending lands inside the last Chapter rather than after everything including it.
- Deleting a Chapter is an archive and touches nothing else. Its Clip Mockups are absorbed upward by the same implicit rule, with no write.

**Core service.** A new operations service for the noun, alongside the Clip Mockup one, offering list-by-Video, get-by-id, create-at-anchor, rename, move-to-anchor and archive. Archived rows are excluded from every read and there is no restore, matching Clip Mockups and Beats. Like the Clip Mockup service it touches no disk and takes no Draft Course Version guard — the guard exists for the published Course Version write-closure, which Clip Mockups sit outside.

**A shared merged read.** Both services need "this Video's Animatic as one ordered list of both kinds of row". That belongs in one place, returning discriminated rows sorted by `order` with the byte-comparison the order keys require, and is what the CLI's `--with-chapters`, the Animatic loader and all four positioning paths read.

**CLI.** A new top-level command, `cvm clip-mockup-chapter`, with `add`, `list`, `get`, `update`, `move`, `delete`. Registered alongside the other nouns; long-form `--help` in its own help module, since the command module must stay inside the repo's per-file token budget. Decisions inside it:

- Chapters are addressed by **bare id only**. No `--at`, no name lookup. A Chapter has no position, so there is nothing for `--at` to count to, and titles are not unique.
- `--title` is the flag, though the column is `name`, so that the two Chapter nouns read identically at the prompt.
- `--before` / `--after` take **any** id in the merged order space — a Clip Mockup or a Chapter — and are mutually exclusive. `add` with neither appends. `move` with neither is invalid input.
- **Not local-only.** Every `cvm clip-mockup` verb is refused off Matt's machine because frames and WAVs are a directory there; a Chapter row touches no disk, so it is allowed everywhere. The asymmetry is deliberate and is stated in the help.
- Exit codes follow the house contract: unknown Video or anchor is not-found, bad flag combinations are invalid input.

**`clip-mockup list --with-chapters`.** An opt-in flag. Off, the stream is unchanged byte for byte, protecting the skill's `jq` pipelines. On, Chapter rows are interleaved in order and **every** row carries two added fields: `type`, one of `clipMockup` / `clipMockupChapter`, and `position` — 1..N over Clip Mockups only, `null` on a Chapter. The explicit position is what stops an agent counting lines and deriving the wrong `--at`.

**The Animatic page.** The loader gains the Video's Chapters and hands the player a list that carries both kinds of row. The playback timeline is untouched: a Chapter is never a Remotion segment, so the frame count, the run time and the position badge are all exactly what they are today. In the sidebar:

- A Chapter renders as a divider with a collapse chevron, its title, and its rolled-up Clip Mockup count and run time, computed from the segments between it and the next divider. An empty Chapter reads as zero and no seconds.
- Clicking the title seeks the playhead to the first Clip Mockup under it. A Chapter with none does not seek.
- Collapsing hides the Clip Mockup rows under that divider and nothing else. Playback is entirely unaffected.
- Collapse state is ephemeral component state, keyed by Chapter id, dying on reload — the same choice the Clip timeline makes, and for the same reason.
- A Chapter auto-expands when the active segment falls inside it, mirroring the Clip timeline's behaviour when the current Clip is inside a collapsed Chapter.
- A single toggle button lives in the sidebar's existing header row, collapsing everything when anything is open and expanding everything when all are closed, using the same pair of icons the Clip timeline uses. It is not rendered when the Video has no Chapters.
- Clip Mockups above the first divider render as plain rows, with no synthetic heading.
- There is no keyboard shortcut; the player already binds space.
- **No UI writes.** The page never creates, renames, moves or deletes a Chapter. Writes are the CLI.

**The grouping arithmetic is pure.** Turning an ordered list of rows plus a playhead into "the Chapters, each with its segments, count, run time and seek frame" is arithmetic over rows, and lives in a pure module beside the existing Animatic timeline arithmetic rather than inside the player component.

**Copy-forward.** Chapters are copied wherever Clip Mockups are: the Course Version snapshot, the duplicated Video and the duplicated Course. The Video-copy path regenerates order keys, so it must generate them across the **merged** list and hand each row back its key in place — copying the two tables independently would pile every divider at one end. Like Clip Mockups, Chapters never reach `course.json`.

**The Mockups tab is deleted.** The tab and its body, the Clip Mockup list component and its line editor, its drag-and-drop stack, its data hook and the editor API route that served it all go, along with the tab's value in the persisted-tab validator and the one test case asserting a persisted `mockups` tab survives. Script was already the default, so nothing moves. Two modules stay because the Animatic loader uses them: the frame/audio URL builder and the asset route that serves the PNG and the WAV. Doc comments in the modules that survive and referred to the list are rewritten rather than left stale.

**Documentation.** A `**Clip Mockup Chapter**` entry in CONTEXT.md under `### Video planning` beside Clip Mockup and Animatic, with an `_Avoid_` line; an added `_Avoid_` line on the existing `**Chapter**` entry so the confusion is guarded from both sides; and an ADR recording the shared-order-space decision, the implicit membership that follows and the deliberate absence of a Beat link. CONTEXT.md and the `--help` prose move together, as CLAUDE.md requires.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a caller can observe — the rows a command prints, the exit code it returns, the order the next read comes back in — and never how a key was computed or which service was called. Existing seams are reused throughout; exactly one new pure seam is introduced.

**The CLI seam carries the feature.** `makeClipMockupRun` plus the PGlite test database runs the real `cvm` program end to end, with only speech synthesis and frame capture faked. Everything behavioural about the noun is asserted there, in a new test file of its own because the per-file token budget will not take it in an existing one:

- `add` appends; `add --before` / `--after` place against a Clip Mockup id and against another Chapter id; a Clip Mockup added afterwards lands **inside** the last Chapter, which is the proof the order space is really shared.
- `move` repositions and refuses with no anchor; `update` renames; `get` behaves as one id and as many.
- `delete` archives the Chapter, and a following `clip-mockup list` shows every Clip Mockup still there — the absorb-upward guarantee, asserted as an outcome rather than a rule.
- `list --with-chapters` interleaves in order, discriminates every row by `type`, numbers Clip Mockups 1..N with Chapters at `null`, and — the regression this is really for — a bare `list` beside it is unchanged.
- The verbs run with the machine **not** declared local, which is the inverse of the assertion `cli-local-only.test.ts` makes about `clip-mockup`.
- Bad input: unknown `--video`, unknown anchor, both anchors at once, each with its house exit code.

**Copy-forward uses the three existing core test seams.** The Course Version copy, Video copy and Course duplicate suites each gain a case seeding an Animatic with Chapters interleaved between Clip Mockups and asserting the copy's merged order reads back in the same sequence — which is the only assertion that catches key regeneration collapsing the interleaving.

**The Animatic grouping is tested as pure arithmetic**, in the style the existing timeline test already uses: no jsdom, no Remotion, no player. Rows in, Chapters with their segments, counts, run times and seek frames out. The cases worth naming are the ones with no Chapters at all, rows above the first Chapter, an empty Chapter, and a Chapter whose rows include an unvoiced hold.

**Deliberately not tested**, with the reason: the collapse state itself. It is component state with the same shape and the same behaviour as the Clip timeline's, which is untested for the same reason — a `useState` of booleans keyed by id asserts nothing a reader does not already see, and the arithmetic it drives is covered above at the pure seam.

**The deletion is verified by subtraction**: the one test case asserting a persisted `mockups` tab is removed with it, the dnd test dies with the module it tested, and the existing editor-header test that asserts the "Watch the Animatic" link still passes, which is what proves the removal did not take the route to the player with it.

## Out of Scope

- Any UI that writes a Clip Mockup Chapter. Creating, renaming, moving and deleting are CLI-only, deliberately.
- Any UI that writes a Clip Mockup at all, once the Mockups tab is gone — no inline line editing, no drag-to-reorder, no delete button anywhere.
- The Chapter title on the player's canvas badge, or anywhere over the frame.
- Chapters as Remotion segments, title cards, or anything else that adds time to the playback.
- Per-Chapter numbering (`2.4`). The position stays a single count over Clip Mockups.
- Any link, field or inference between a Clip Mockup Chapter and a Beat, in either direction.
- Persisted or shared collapse state.
- A keyboard shortcut for collapsing, and next/previous-Chapter seeking.
- A restore verb for a deleted Chapter.
- Reading or writing Clip Mockup Chapters from `course.json`, or any change to the published Course at all.
- Moving a Clip Mockup Chapter between Videos.
- Any change to the real `chapter` table, its CLI or the Clip timeline.

## Further Notes

The wiki-side half of this cannot be in the same PR, because the `animatic` skill lives in a different repository. It is a companion change in `mattpocock/personal-wiki`: the skill gains a section teaching the noun, the CLI surface, `--with-chapters` as the way to read an Animatic back, and the YouTube-chapter framing — coarse, navigational, named for a viewer, with no granularity rule and explicitly no mirroring of the Beats.

Two existing statements in CONTEXT.md need reading alongside the new entry rather than contradicting it. "There is no Animatic record" stays true: a Clip Mockup Chapter belongs to a Video, not to an Animatic, and nothing is addressed by the word Animatic. And "a Clip Mockup does not point at a Beat" stays true and is the reason the skill must not smuggle a Beat link back in through a title.

The asymmetry in local-only is the one thing in this design a reader will trip over: `cvm clip-mockup-chapter list` works on the Remote Box while `cvm clip-mockup list` beside it is refused. It is intentional — the frames and the WAVs are a directory on one machine, a Chapter is a row — and it is worth stating in the `--help` where a confused agent will actually read it.

issues.title: Clip Mockup Chapters: the noun, one shared order space, and add/list
issues.body:
## Parent

#1723 — Clip Mockup Chapters for the Animatic, and delete the Mockups tab

## What to build

The new noun, and the one decision the whole feature rests on: a **Clip Mockup Chapter** is a named divider in a Video's Animatic that shares **one fractional order key space** with its Clip Mockups — exactly as a Chapter shares one with a Clip.

Membership is therefore implicit: a Clip Mockup belongs to the last Chapter above it, there is no `chapterId` on a Clip Mockup, and nothing needs re-parenting when a row moves. Clip Mockups above the first divider belong to no Chapter.

This ticket delivers the noun end to end as far as `add` and `list`, so it is demoable at the prompt:

```
cvm clip-mockup-chapter add  --video <id> --title "…" [--before <id> | --after <id>]
cvm clip-mockup-chapter list --video <id>
```

`add` with no anchor appends to the end of the Animatic. `--before` / `--after` are mutually exclusive and accept **any** id in the merged order space — a Clip Mockup id or another Chapter id.

The part that makes the shared order space real rather than nominal: **creating or moving a Clip Mockup must compute its key against the merged, sorted list of both nouns.** Its external behaviour is unchanged — append to the end, or before a named row — but appending now lands *inside* the last Chapter instead of after everything including it. The repo already has the positioning primitive that does this for Clips and Chapters; reuse it rather than writing a second one.

Also in scope: the `clip_mockup_chapter` table and its migration (Video-owned, cascade delete, indexed like every other Video-owned noun, `archived` with no restore), the core operations service beside the Clip Mockup one, and the one shared merged read — "this Video's Animatic as one ordered list of both kinds of row", sorted with the byte comparison the order keys require — that the CLI, the Animatic loader and all four positioning paths will use.

Two deliberate differences from the real Chapter: **no Draft Course Version guard** (Clip Mockups sit outside that write-closure, and their grouping follows them), and **not local-only** (every `cvm clip-mockup` verb is refused off Matt's machine because frames and WAVs are a directory there; a Chapter row touches no disk). Both are stated in `--help`, where a confused agent will actually read them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cvm clip-mockup-chapter add --video <id> --title "…"` appends a Chapter and echoes the created row.
- [ ] `--before <id>` and `--after <id>` place a Chapter against a Clip Mockup id *and* against another Chapter id; both flags together is invalid input.
- [ ] `cvm clip-mockup-chapter list --video <id>` prints the Video's active Chapters as NDJSON in order; an empty list prints nothing and exits 0.
- [ ] A Clip Mockup added after a Chapter exists lands **inside** that Chapter — i.e. its order key sorts after the divider — which is the assertion that proves one shared order space.
- [ ] Existing `cvm clip-mockup add` / `move` behaviour is otherwise unchanged; their tests still pass untouched.
- [ ] An unknown `--video` is a not-found with the house exit code; an unknown anchor likewise.
- [ ] Every verb runs with the machine **not** declared local, the inverse of what the local-only suite asserts about `clip-mockup`.
- [ ] No Draft Course Version is required for any write.
- [ ] `cvm clip-mockup-chapter --help` explains the noun, implicit membership, the shared order space, and both deliberate asymmetries.
- [ ] Covered at the existing CLI seam (`makeClipMockupRun` + the PGlite test database) in a new test file of its own, since the per-file token budget will not take it in an existing one.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).

issues.title: Remove the local-repo backing entirely — no feature flag, no new repo-backed courses
issues.body:
## Question

Should CVM keep any form of the local git-repo / `CourseRepo` backing of courses — the on-disk section/lesson folders, the ghost/real distinction, the materialization cascade, and the git plumbing — possibly behind a mode or feature flag, or remove it wholesale?

issues.title: Publish output: .mp4 + course.json only, drop all markdown sidecars
issues.body:
## Question

Once the repo is gone, what does **Publish** emit to Dropbox, and does `course.json` need to grow new fields (notably transcript) to stay the complete published artifact?

issues.title: Keep todo/done as a free per-lesson flag; keep the in-app changelog
issues.body:
## Question

`authoringStatus` (`todo`/`done`) is welded to `fsStatus` by a DB biconditional CHECK (real ⇔ has a status, ghost ⇔ null). When `fsStatus` disappears, do we keep `todo`/`done` or drop it? And what happens to the changelog, which reads it?

issues.title: Unify per-video local files across all videos, keyed by lineageId
issues.body:
## Question

With lessons no longer backed by on-disk folders, where do a video's **local files** (writing-agent source material, thumbnails, screenshots, uploads) live — and how do we avoid duplicating them when Publish clones every video into a new course version?

issues.title: Migration: DB-only drops + rename standalone dirs to lineageId; leave repos untouched
issues.body:
## Question

What does the one-time migration do — to the schema, to the existing on-disk course repos, and to stale Dropbox output from past publishes?

issues.title: Sequencing with #1190 title-driven paths: land slices 1-3, cancel 4 & 6
issues.body:
## Question

How does this effort sequence with the in-flight title-driven-paths work (PR #1190 / map #1181), which is actively being built and partly overlaps?

issues.title: Agent VFS model without ghost/real or materialize
issues.body:
## Question

The course-editing **agent** operates over a VFS (`app/services/vfs/vfs-loader.server.ts`, `agent-diff-executor.ts`) that surfaces `ghost`/`real` on lessons/sections and gates *materialize* on `course.filePath === null`. With no filesystem and everything DB-only, what is the agent's model?

- Does the agent still create/edit **sections, lessons, videos** purely as DB rows (no materialize/dematerialize verbs)?
- Does it read/write **per-video local files** (now `video-files/{lineageId}`), and if so through what VFS surface?
- What happens to the in-memory **agent `course.json`** (the VFS one, distinct from the published artifact) and its `ghost`/materialize affordances / `[ghost]` tags?

Output: the agent's post-removal VFS contract — what it can see and change — precise enough to spec the `vfs-*` and `agent-diff-executor` changes.

issues.title: Confirm no live dependency on git-push to a student repo
issues.body:
## Question

Killing the repo removes `git-push` (`api.courses.$courseId.git-push.ts`) and with it the ability to re-publish an old course **together with its student-facing GitHub repo** — the original reason this coupling existed ("courses tightly coupled to a skills-building repo").

Confirm no current or near-future course depends on pushing to a cohort/student repo, and decide whether anything replaces it — or whether old repos simply stay **inert on disk**, edited by hand in the rare case an old course needs a repo update.

issues.title: course.json path shape now that it's CMS-facing, not folder-facing
issues.body:
## Question

#1181 derived a section/lesson `path` as a number-prefixed slug (`NN-slug` / `NN.MM-slug`) **because it was an on-disk folder name** needing filesystem ordering and uniqueness. With no folders, `course.json` `path` becomes a purely **CMS-facing identifier**.

Do we keep the numeric prefixes, switch to clean slugs, or something else? Confirm the `course.json` `path` contract the future AI Hero importer will target. (May resolve to "keep #1181's derivation unchanged" — but repo-removal legitimately reopens it.)
